Overview › Pantry

Pantry

The household's ingredient ledger and everything that feeds it: single and batch add with canonical resolution, the bought→pantry hand-off from shopping, starter staples, prepared dishes with storage-driven expiry — plus the one honest number it serves the home screen ("puedes cocinar X de Y", allergen-safe by construction). The receipt bridge the pantry was named for is deferred: today nothing enters without a human confirming it.

Docs The feature card

the entity in one handle, one analogy and one constraint box

Authored in cards/pantry.md — the only hand-written source on this page. Everything counted elsewhere is read from the codebase at build time.

“"Everything in your kitchen, by canonical name — and what those items let you cook tonight."”

ISthe pantry inventory (items, locations, staples, expiry), its append-only history ledger, the shopping→pantry confirmation flow, and the cookability projection served on the overview.
IS NOTthe recipe availability engine's internals (recipe entity code) — the pantry consumes compute_recipe_availability; and not the receipt-ingest bridge, which exists as a walled mock (D43).
DECIDESwhat counts as "in the pantry" (active, canonical-coded, quantity-positive), where each item lives, when a prepared dish expires, and which deletion reason writes history.

a well-run restaurant storeroom — everything logged in the ledger under its catalog name (never the supplier's scribble), shelves labeled (one principal shelf that can't be removed), a "use soon" board for prepared trays, and a chalkboard out front: "tonight we can plate 22 of the 302 dishes on OUR menu" — dishes the house can't safely serve were never on that menu.

AnalogyIn this codebase
storeroom ledgerapps/api/models/pantry.py:32, :83
intake deskapps/api/api/pantry.py:125, :139, :205
delivery hand-offapps/api/services/shopping.py:401
chalkboard numberapps/api/services/recipe_availability.py:76
use-soon boardapps/api/services/cooking.py:603-618, apps/web/src/features/pantry/screens/PantryScreen.tsx:333-347

Easy to confuse:

  • the receipt-fed promise (SC-01) — the ingest service exists (ingest_receipt_items) but mapped items are counted and NEVER appended (D43); the real Gastify client raises ProviderNotWiredError.
  • prepared dishes vs ingredients — kind='prepared' rows never satisfy a recipe (get_pantry_ingredient_codes filters kind='ingredient'); they exist for eating and expiry, not cooking.

Where the analogy stops working: the storeroom analogy breaks at the chalkboard — the denominator differs per household (allergen-safe catalog, D158); two houses genuinely have different menus, and that is the feature.

Full card — what & why, for whom, flows, is / is not

What & Why

The pantry is the entry of the plan→buy→cook loop (SCOPE SC-01/REQ-01): a household-gated inventory where every row references a canonical ingredient code (D1 — raw grocery strings never stored). It is fed by four confirmed paths — single add (api/pantry.py:125), batch add with deterministic candidate resolution and per-row savepoint isolation (D101; :139/:205), the shopping bought-confirmation (Flow2 — confirm_bought atomically flips the shopping row, creates the PantryItem, and appends a compra history event, services/shopping.py:401), and starter staples (batch-added to the principal Despensa). Cooking completion writes back: a stored leftover becomes a prepared item whose expiry_date derives from its storage method's shelf life (D115/D121, services/cooking.py:603-618), surfaced by the "por vencer" banner whose tap-through pre-seeds the expiry filter — with expired rows bucketed into today so the filter cannot hide the very item the banner announced (F2.3.1/D159, PantryScreenModel.ts:370-374). The overview also serves the home screen's one honest number: cookable_count/catalog_total composes the allergen wall FIRST, availability second (D158, services/recipe_availability.py:76) — the ratio can never advertise a recipe that could hurt the household. Every mutation lands in the append-only IngredientHistoryEvent ledger (compra/receta/descarte/consumo). The receipt bridge the app was designed around is explicitly deferred (D43): mapped receipt items are counted as mapped_pending and not appended (services/receipt_ingest.py:68-71); unmapped ones queue for admin review.

For Whom

  • The household cook — adds what they bought (typed, batch-resolved, or one tap from shopping), sees what's about to expire before it's wasted, and reads one trustworthy "you can cook X of Y" on the home screen.
  • The co-cook — the same household inventory, locations, and expiry board; nothing is per-user except who added it.
  • The allergic household — the cookability denominator is THEIR safe catalog; the chalkboard never counts a dish that could hurt them (D158's live probe: 26/550 cleared vs 22/302 lactose-free vs 22/263 +fish).
  • The future receipt user — the SC-01 promise holder; the contract and admin-review queue exist, the bridge waits on Gastify readiness (D43).

Flows

  • add ★ → single add (api/pantry.py:125) and batch: resolve-batch ranks canonical candidates read-only (:139), the confirmed rows create in ONE txn with per-row savepoints (D101, :205); staples checklist batch-adds to the principal Despensa; expiry is user-supplied at add time and carried through create (C5 fix, pantryModel.ts:317). (assured: test_batch_add 15 cases + test_pantry 19 in the api corpus)
  • bought-to-pantry → Flow2: POST /shopping/items/{id}/confirm-bought (api/shopping.py:114) → confirm_bought atomic multi-write (services/shopping.py:401) — replay-tolerant; the web then patches qty/unit/location from the confirmation sheet (ShoppingContainer.tsx:95-108).
  • overview → GET /pantry/overview (api/pantry.py:84): active items with locale-aware display names (D111) + cookable_count/catalog_total (D158 wall-first, services/recipe_availability.py:76). (assured: test_cookability_summary 6 cases; live two-direction probe in the cookability proof set)
  • expiry → prepared items expire by storage-method shelf life (services/cooking.py:603-618); the banner routes to a pre-seeded Preparados expiry filter and Vencido buckets into today so the announced item stays visible (F2.3.1/D159). (assured: expiryRouting.test.tsx C1446-C1452 + the storage-batch journey; proof set expiry-routing, 4 legs)
  • organize → locations CRUD (principal Despensa: partial-unique index, delete blocked 409, orphaned items reassigned to principal before delete — services/locations.py); pantry reset preview/apply (idempotency-keyed, keep/discard/move per item). Since P5b the ORDER and the "Activa" flag are server state too (locations.display_order + .active, migration 0062 / D184): the two controls that used to write browser state only now PATCH like rename does, and hiding the principal is refused 409 exactly as deleting it is. (assured: C8110-C8113 api + C8114/C8115/C8118/C8123/C8124 web; proof set myopic-c6-location-order-active, 2 legs)
  • repertorio → Preparados reworked as the cupo's home surface (P6 spike, RepertorioSpike.tsx over the REAL PantryItemRow/ConfirmDialog): prepared stock groups by dish TYPE, solid cards are the HOUSEHOLD's stock and ghost cards are the VIEWER's unfilled cupos with a type-scoped "descubrir" CTA — so two members of one household see the same solids and different ghosts (D182). Shipped as Storybook only; the live surface is the recipe entity's cupo/sugerencias flows. (assured: repertorioModel + sugerenciasModel tests in the web corpus; proof set f6-repertorio-spike, role reference)
  • history → GET /pantry/history: the append-only IngredientHistoryEvent ledger — compra/receta/descarte/consumo with display-name snapshots.
  • receipt-dormant → ingest_receipt_items (services/receipt_ingest.py:24): idempotent by (household, request_id); not_found → AdminReviewQueue; mapped → counted mapped_pending, NOT appended (D43); the real Boletapp client raises ProviderNotWiredError (integrations/gastify_exchange.py:93). Contract proven by test_gastify_contract.

Is

  • Canonical-coded by construction (D1): PantryItem.ingredient_code references the catalog; the web resolves Spanish typing to codes via curated + taxonomy-derived aliases (ingredientAliases.ts:155).
  • Household-scoped everywhere: every route passes ctx.require_household(); items, locations, history, and resets are household facts, not user facts.
  • Two kinds, one table: kind='ingredient' feeds cooking; kind='prepared' feeds eating + expiry and NEVER satisfies a recipe (services/recipe_availability.py:22 filters kind).
  • Soft-delete with a reason (D98): used → consumo history, removed → discard; both leave the ledger intact.
  • The cookability number is safety-composed (D158): allergen wall first, availability second — reused via compute_cookability_summary, never recomposed over raw ids.
  • A location's arrangement is durable (D184, migration 0062): display_order and active persist, so the shelf order a household builds survives a reload. Reordering is TWO-SIDED — taking a slot moves whoever held it (C8123) — and hiding a location that still holds items says where those items went rather than silently emptying a screen (C8124).
  • kind='prepared' survives creation now (#121, C8133): the batch add path silently DROPPED the kind and wrote every row as an ingredient, so prepared food added in bulk could never expire or fill a cupo. Fixed in both layers plus the web sheet — the same silent-failure-fake-success class as C5's dropped expiry.
  • One expiry surface, not two (#120, C8137): the duplicated Despensa expiry views were merged, so the banner and the section can no longer disagree about what is expiring.
  • Reset is idempotency-keyed (PantryResetOperation unique on household+key) with a dry-run preview.

Is Not

  • not receipt-fed today — SC-01's "no manual typing" is a deferred promise (D43); every current entry path involves a human confirming.
  • not the availability engine — compute_recipe_availability belongs to the recipe entity; the pantry consumes its projection.
  • not a per-user pantry — there is exactly one per household; added_by_user_id is provenance, not ownership.
  • not a shopping list — shopping rows live in their own domain; only confirm_bought crosses the boundary, atomically.
  • not a drag-to-sort surface — the order is a slot picker, and the badge you see is a RE-DERIVED display position (normalizePantryLocationOrders), not the stored number. The two are allowed to differ; only the stored value is the household's arrangement.
  • hiding a location is not deleting it — an inactive location leaves the Ubicaciones view, but its items stay listed under Ingredientes and Preparados, and it can be reactivated.

Docs Changelog — decisions that shaped it

why the entity behaves the way it does

Source: the entity card's DECIDED section. A decision here is a rule the code obeys, not a plan — the ones with ids are in .kdbp/DECISIONS.md.

DecisionWhat it settles
D1canonical codes only: raw grocery strings never stored; Spanish typing resolves through curated + taxonomy aliases before any write.
D43receipt auto-populate deferred: mapped items counted (mapped_pending), never appended; real Gastify client raises until the bridge is ready.
D98deletion carries a reason (used/removed) and locations carry builder color/icon; the detail sheet is editable in live.
D101batch add is one txn with per-row savepoints: one bad row 422s alone, the rest land.
D111locale-aware display names on overview/resolve/frequent (display_es|display_en by user language).
D115/D121storage-method-driven prepared expiry (refrigerar/congelar/despensa shelf lives; string codes, not DB enums; expired stays visible, never a hard block).
D158cookability composes the allergen wall FIRST; catalog_total is the SAFE total; any new cookable consumer must reuse compute_cookability_summary.
F2.3.1/D159expiry announcements route to where you act: banner/card tap pre-seeds the filter; Vencido buckets into today so the filter can't hide the announced item.
C5the add-sheet's expiry reaches the create body (was silently dropped — the data-loss class this repo names "silent-failure-fake-success").
D84/D85flat bodies + coarse pantry.all invalidation on every mutation.
D184C6 gets BUILT, not hidden: the myopic walk found the reorder badge and the "Activa" toggle writing browser state only, so an arrangement died on reload. The ruling was to give them a server home rather than remove them. active is NOT NULL default TRUE (a nullable column would have handed every pre-0062 location a NULL against a bool schema and stopped the pantry rendering); display_order is nullable with NO backfill, because a location nobody has arranged has no honest position and a backfilled 1 would invent one.
D182the cupo blend is deliberately split-scoped: solid cards read HOUSEHOLD stock, ghosts and counters read the VIEWER. A shared pantry with a personal repertoire is the point; rendering either half at the wrong scope would make one member's progress look like another's.
D183a released cupo costs something and must say so first; the Preparados surface owns that prompt because it is where the ghosts live.
—The principal is protected the same way twice: it cannot be DELETED and it cannot be HIDDEN, both 409. Every un-located item falls back to it, so hiding it would strand rows the user can no longer reach — the same hole as deleting it, entered by a different door.

Code Data model

DB entities and API shapes — each names its file and the endpoints that touch it

A field typed with another documented class LINKS to it (violet) instead of repeating its structure. Examples are synthetic — derived from Literal values and field-name heuristics, never real user data.
Type colors — one hue per family, deeper = the wider type: int float · Decimal numeric · date · time datetime temporal · str bytes · Text textual · bool · list · dict · Literal structured · UUID identity · None nullable. An uncolored token is a domain alias (an enum defined in this codebase).
Insight icons — the DATA-MODEL lens; the same shape runs over other member kinds later (functions · methods), scoped, never mixed:
  • model — a persisted DB entity: lives in a table, owns FKs.
  • schema — an API / pipeline shape: crosses a boundary, owns no storage.
  • base — derives from NOTHING: no FK out, no field typed by another documented class; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-class flag — field count ≥ 15; the number that makes it a split candidate below.
  • Class N% closest structural twin — % = shared fields over the union (Jaccard); a ≥80% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoint touches + FK in) · violet = internal (mapped backend files referencing the class). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: they count references inside the config-mapped files only, so a zero means no indexed usage — go check, never dead. One unmapped file falsifies a zero; nothing falsifies a count.

About this section

The API surface is api/pantry.py (overview/items/batch/locations/reset/history/frequent) and the bought-confirmation in api/shopping.py. Services: services/pantry.py (CRUD + history), services/shopping.py (Flow2 atomic write + list generation), services/locations.py (principal protection + orphan reassignment), services/pantry_reset.py (idempotent keep/discard/move), services/receipt_ingest.py (the walled D43 bridge) with integrations/gastify_exchange.py + schemas/gastify.py (the cross-app contract), and the pantry-facing cookability trio in services/recipe_availability.py. Data: models/pantry.py (PantryItem, IngredientHistoryEvent, reset tables), models/location.py (principal partial-unique, color/icon/type). The web core is PantryContainer.tsx → screens/PantryScreen.tsx/PantryViews.tsx, the add flows (components/add/PantryAddSheet.tsx, components/batch/* + useBatchAdd.ts, model/PantryAddCatalog.ts, staples under components/staples/), inventory (components/inventory/PantryItemDetailSheet.tsx editable-in-live, PantryItemRow.tsx), the expiry surfaces (components/PantryExpiryBanner.tsx + the routing in PantryScreen.tsx/PantryScreenModel.ts), models (pantryModel.ts, model/PantryScreenModel.ts, model/PantryLocationModel.ts, model/pantryTaxonomy.ts, model/ingredientAliases.ts), hooks (usePantryOverview/Mutations/Locations/History.ts), and the shopping hand-off UI (features/shopping/*).

Code Data-model candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; the verdict lands in DECISIONS/PENDING via review or a health pass, never here

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — structural twins ≥ 80% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god class ≥ 15 fields (from the N fields flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing uses this" — similarity and size are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped classes sharing 87% of their field names is TRUE no matter what lives outside the map, and a 22-field class is 22 fields however little the config covers. Absence of references is neither — a single file outside the entity config falsifies it. This section names only what the instrument can actually support. The usage evidence lives on the Data model page — two bars per class, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per class only, only above the 50% line, Python only, mapped files only, and only field NAMES (types and semantics are not compared). Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. This TABLE cuts higher still — it lists pairs at ≥ 80%, so the 50% recording floor is what the flag sees, not what you are reading. This page is a FLOOR, not a census: it under-reports duplication and always will. That direction is the safe one — under-reporting a positive signal costs you a missed merge; under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — classes outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can carry near-identical schemas and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.

Insight icons — the FUNCTIONS lens:
  • function — a module-level def.
  • method — a def bound to a class.
  • endpoint handler — a route decorator serves it.
  • base — calls no other documented function; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-function flag — length ≥ 50 lines; makes it a split candidate below.
  • fn N% closest structural twin — body-identifier overlap (Jaccard); a ≥85% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoints served + api-layer files referencing) · violet = internal (mapped files referencing — same-file calls outside the def count: a helper used within its module is used). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: the scan reads config-mapped Python only, so a zero reads no indexed caller — go check, never dead.

Code Function candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; same contract as the data-model candidates, function-scoped

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — identifier twins ≥ 85% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god function ≥ 50 lines (from the N length flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing calls this" — similarity and length are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped defs sharing 87% of their body identifiers is TRUE regardless of what lies outside the map, and a 120-line function is 120 lines however little the config covers. "Nothing references this" is falsified by one file outside the corpus — so this section names duplication and size, and never asserts deadness. The usage evidence lives on the Functions page — two bars per def, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per def, only among defs with ≥ 8 body identifiers, only above the 60% line, Python only, mapped files only — while this TABLE cuts higher still, listing pairs at ≥ 85%. Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. The page is a FLOOR, not a census — and that direction is the safe one: under-reporting a positive signal costs a missed merge, while under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — files outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can share dozens of byte-identical functions and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.

A set is one directory under tests/web-e2e/proof/; its manifest.json supplies the story and the leg names, the file counts are walked off disk. The ROLE column says where each set sits in the entity's story — derived from the card's # FLOWS and the manifest (an explicit role:/flows: in the manifest overrides the inference; an inferred role says so). A ★ in the card's FLOWS marks the GOLDEN PATH — this feature's own main journey; a set covering a ★ flow wears the star, and an unproven ★ flow is the loudest gap on the shelf. Open a row to see its legs, then click any artifact to open the viewer — ← / → or the side arrows run through the WHOLE set, leg by leg; ↑ / ↓ move to the previous or next set (folding this one shut and unfolding that one); Esc closes. Opening or closing a set cascades to its legs.

claims the legacy pages made that this page refuses to repeat, and why

Claims adjacent legacy material made that this card refuses to repeat as pantry facts:

  • "pantry from receipt ingest, no manual typing" as a current capability (SCOPE SC-01 shorthand) — deferred, not built: mapped receipt items are counted and dropped (receipt_ingest.py:68-71); the real client is walled (ProviderNotWiredError). The contract and admin queue exist; the append does not.
  • "cookable-count is a pantry-only fact" (cookable-count card placement) — qualified: the number is SERVED on /pantry/overview but computed by the recipe entity's compute_cookability_summary; D158's review trigger (any new consumer must reuse it) is the recipe entity's invariant, referenced here.
  • "expiry lives in the pantry service" — dropped: prepared-dish expiry is written by the COOKING completion path (services/cooking.py:603-618) from taxonomy shelf-life; ingredient expiry is user-supplied at add. The pantry renders and routes; it does not compute shelf life.
